comparison: Perfect agreement on fabrication methodology (C59-C61). Both evaluations support the molding process and manufacturing approach. Peer review notes the method is 'practical and easy to adopt' and that initial concerns about manufacturing yield were addressed.

Perfect agreement on experimental PSF measurements (C62-C68). Both support the quantitative validation showing improved optical performance. Peer review emphasizes 'convincing evidence' of significantly increased field of view and reduced aberrations.

Perfect agreement on morphological imaging results (C69-C70). Both evaluations support improved cellular resolution across FOV. Peer review explicitly confirms 'optical resolution is maintained over a larger field of view' with neuronal processes visible at FOV edges.

Perfect agreement on simulation-experiment discrepancies (C89-C91). Both support the authors' explanations for differences. Peer review notes initial concerns were 'adequately addressed' with explanations of differences between ex vivo and in vivo conditions.

Perfect agreement on background claims about GRIN lens limitations (C2-C5, C27-C31). Both evaluations support these foundational claims establishing the problem. Peer review confirms these as accepted background with no challenges raised.

Strong agreement on simulation methodology (C43-C58). Both support the optical design and simulation approach. OpenEval covers additional claims (C53) not explicitly mentioned in peer review. Peer reviewers describe simulations as 'clear and thorough.'

Partial overlap on synthetic calcium imaging simulations. OpenEval focuses on simulation framework and statistical methods (C71-C74), while peer review addresses both simulation benefits (C71-C74) and GLM analysis results (C75-C80, C98-C99). Both strongly support the findings with peer review noting 'significantly stronger correlation with ground truth.'

Partial overlap on signal quality analysis. OpenEval focuses on GLM analysis and source mixing quantification (C75-C80), while peer review groups this with simulation results and includes additional claims (C71-C74, C98-C99). Both evaluations support the reduced cross-contamination findings.

Strong agreement on in vivo validation (C81-C86). Both support the statistical analysis and biological findings. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and distance-dependent correlations. Peer review notes successful measurements 'from large numbers of cells simultaneously in vivo' and that basic analysis of odor responses addressed initial concerns. Peer review also includes broader impact claims (C105-C107).

Partial overlap on research implications. OpenEval addresses broader research implications (C105-C113), while peer review focuses on successful in vivo demonstration (C81-C86, C105-C107). Both support the claims, with peer review emphasizing practical achievement in 'difficult preparation.'

Partial overlap on methodological advantages. OpenEval covers comparison with alternative methods and advantages (C32-C42, C114-C116), while peer review emphasizes the no-modification advantage (C40, C114-C116, C118). Both strongly support these claims with peer review noting this as 'main strength' across multiple reviewers.

Partial overlap on positioning relative to prior work. OpenEval addresses gap identification and comparison with alternatives (C32-C42, C114-C116), while peer review focuses on extension from prior work (C6-C7, C39, C41-C42). Both support the claims with peer review noting this 'closely follows earlier work' and extends to longer lenses.

Partial overlap on technical specifications and impact. OpenEval addresses specifications and forward-looking claims (C88, C117-C119), while peer review emphasizes practical adoption and value (C9, C13, C88, C117). Both support the claims with peer review describing as 'valuable study' and 'potentially key method.'

Minimal overlap on ease of adoption. OpenEval mentions combination of features (C117-C118), while peer review emphasizes no-modification requirement (C40, C114-C116, C118). Both support these advantages.

Minimal overlap on curved focal plane. OpenEval addresses curved focal plane characteristics (C96-C104), while peer review briefly mentions this (C98-C99) within broader simulation discussion. Both support the claims as valid trade-offs.

OpenEval addresses experimental design controls with coverslips (C92-C95) and speculation about improvement versus bare GRIN lenses. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific methodological details.
